November 16, 2026

Officials relocated to military bases over reported Iranian drone plot

tags: politics, defence
sources: @ericmoutsos, @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy

Israeli intelligence passed a warning to the CIA that Iran was planning a drone swarm attack targeting President Trump and senior officials, according to reports attributed to Mossad and the outlet Israel Hayom. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and Attorney General Todd Blanche have been reported living on U.S. military bases, and Trump's public appearances have been curtailed. The warning was said to be corroborated by a second Western intelligence agency that was not named. Separately, Mossad chief Roman Goffman travelled to Washington to meet senior administration officials and press for a resumption of the war against Iran.

FAA orders nationwide ground stop after air traffic communications failure

tags: politics, tech
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy, @hunteralexanderhowell, @carolinegleich, @ericmoutsos

The Federal Aviation Administration halted all departures at U.S. airports on Friday 13 November, citing "extraordinary circumstances" and reasons of safety, in only the third nationwide ground stop in U.S. history after 9/11 and January 2023. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a contractor's router replacement in El Dorado, Arkansas triggered a Texas router to flood air traffic centers with data; about 60 similar routers have been disabled and officials say there is no evidence of a cyberattack. Three days of fallout produced 17,822 cancellations, with Duffy requesting $50 billion for system upgrades after earlier figures of $30 billion. Air traffic controllers interviewed by a reporter disputed the official account, and critics noted the administration fired hundreds of FAA support staff in 2025 while a congressional watchdog warned in September that the overhaul had no reliable cost estimate or master schedule.

Army officer files whistleblower complaint over drone attack that killed six soldiers

tags: defence, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Army Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom has filed a complaint with Congress alleging that military leaders dismissed his warnings about aerial protection at Port Shuaiba, Kuwait, before an Iranian drone attack killed six U.S. service members on 1 March. He said he raised concerns with superiors and was told "we don't have to worry about protection," and called the event a tactical failure by the Army, its leadership and himself. The Pentagon declined to comment. The complaint became public as Trump posted an apparently AI-generated video of troops praying.

Trump says he takes no responsibility for nationwide ground stop

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy, @oafnation_actual

Trump made no public statement for days after the ground stop and had no entries on his public schedule, while cabinet secretaries Sean Duffy and Markwayne Mullin fronted a press conference that gave conflicting explanations. When reporters later asked whether he had been focused on White House construction projects rather than failing airline systems, he blamed Biden for the airspace problems, said he took no responsibility for the ground stop that left over a million travelers stranded, and attacked the reporter. He said he had been holding meetings in the White House at the time and added that Russia could be tougher on Ukraine.

Iran strikes US base in Bahrain with drones

tags: war, politics
sources: @groundnews

Bahrain's military said it intercepted several Iranian attacks on Sunday before they reached their targets, its first interceptions since September, and accused Iran of a "systematic hostile approach." Iran's Revolutionary Guards said six drones targeted U.S. radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base in response to hostile U.S. actions. Bahrain hosts the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet. Talks have not produced a deal to end the war, which began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

Trump to meet Xi and Putin in first three-way sit-down

tags: politics, defence
sources: @groundnews

The White House confirmed that Trump will join China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin on Thursday during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. A senior U.S. official said the meeting could open nuclear arms talks among the three countries, that no deals were expected, and that Trump planned to discuss the war with Iran while avoiding Ukraine. Trump wants China included in a nuclear pact after New START expired in February, ending limits on the U.S. and Russian arsenals. Pentagon estimates put China's stockpile above 600 warheads against more than 5,000 each for Russia and the United States.

Third US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East

tags: war, defence
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Al Jazeera reported that the USS Theodore Roosevelt has reached the Middle East, making it the third U.S. aircraft carrier deployed to the region. The deployment coincided with Trump reposting a message asking God to protect U.S. troops alongside a video that appears to be AI-generated. Senior administration officials have been moved to military bases over reported Iranian threats.

Iran says supertanker sank after striking mine in Strait of Hormuz

tags: war, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers struck mines on an unauthorized route in the southern Strait of Hormuz and that one, a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude, sank in the Gulf. The Guards named no vessels and there was no independent confirmation. The U.S. military says it has cleared the main routes of mines.

Republican senators block Trump judicial nominees as Alito warns of Democratic Congress

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Senators John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina are blocking judicial nominees from their states, slowing the White House's effort to confirm lifetime appointments before Democrats take control of the Senate. Justice Samuel Alito told a Federalist Society dinner that Democrats leading Congress hold the power of the purse and could, in effect, turn the lights off at the Supreme Court. With a Democratic Senate, it appears no judge or justice will be confirmed over the next two years.

Hegseth says international law should not constrain US military

tags: defence, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said people should stop quoting laws to men with swords, arguing in effect that the U.S. military should not have to abide by international law. The remark responded to Marco Rubio's comments about the International Criminal Court and its work holding war criminals accountable. The same military has been accused of a strike in Iran that killed more than a hundred people at an all-girls school.

Nvidia chief resigns amid China export control and spy scandal

tags: tech, politics
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual, @carolinegleich

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO after news of his affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence suspects of spying for China. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Treasury, State, Defense and the U.S. Trade Representative had backed export restrictions on Singapore-based Megaspeed for months and blamed the Commerce Department, which the New York Times reported had opposed tighter curbs under Secretary Howard Lutnick. A Reuters review of more than 150 procurement notices found $3.2 billion in Chinese AI projects designed around restricted H100, H200 and H800 processors.

Senate nears vote on permitting bill that would fast-track data centers and gas plants

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

The Senate could hold a final vote this week on BAAJA, a permitting bill co-written by Utah Senator Mike Lee that would speed approvals for gas pipelines, gas power plants and the data centers they supply. It would give communities as little as 150 days to challenge a project in court, and tribal leaders and several senators warn it would weaken protections for sacred and cultural sites. Supporters say the bill makes data centers pay their fair share of power costs. Opponents argue the decision should wait for the Congress elected this month, which takes office in January.

United States loses measles elimination status

tags: health
sources: @oafnation_actual

The United States has lost its measles elimination status following continuous local transmission of the virus. The designation lapsed after a resurgence of outbreaks lasting longer than twelve months.

Questions raised over FAA air traffic contract awarded to donor-linked AI firm

tags: politics, tech
sources: @ericmoutsos

Boston-based AI startup Air Space Intelligence donated to the congressional campaign of 26-year-old Michael Alfonso in March, and in June the Transportation Department under Secretary Sean Duffy awarded the company a 12-year contract worth up to $875.9 million to build an AI air traffic tool called SMART. Alfonso, who won a seat in Congress and is sworn in on 3 January, is Duffy's son-in-law. The FAA rolled the software out across 22 air traffic centers on 10 November, three days before the nationwide ground stop. The company says its software had nothing to do with the failure.

Microsoft 365 outage hits governments and hospitals as CISA runs short-staffed

tags: tech, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

A global Microsoft 365 outage entered a second day on Friday, disrupting Outlook and Teams for governments, hospitals and businesses, including U.S. House staff, the Los Angeles County Sheriff and NHS hospitals. Microsoft said there was no evidence of malicious activity. The disruption came as the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, responsible for protecting critical infrastructure, operates with about a third fewer staff after the administration cut roughly 1,000 employees.

US becomes first country to skip UN human rights review

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

The United States is set to become the first country to fully opt out of a U.N. Human Rights Council review of its rights record since the council began work two decades ago. The council rescheduled the review for Tuesday after Washington missed its November 2025 appointment. The Trump administration withdrew from the council in 2025, accusing it of bias against the United States and Israel, and a State Department spokesperson said it gives the agency no credibility. The council reviews all 193 member states on a four- to five-year cycle and says a review requires the country's representatives.

Alaska elects first Democratic governor since 1998

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, won Alaska's race for governor, beating three Republicans including a candidate backed by Trump. Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski backed Kreiss-Tomkins, who campaigned on household costs and full funding for public schools. The result brings Democrats to 30 governorships after midterm gains in states including Georgia and Texas.

Texas Democrats move to roll back Republican policies after midterm wins

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Texas Democrats have begun introducing legislation to undo Republican measures in the state, including ending the required display of the Ten Commandments in schools. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa is prioritising a pay raise for teachers across the state. Democrats also plan to roll back the state's Confederate Heroes Day, observed each January.

Campaign urges open contest for House Democratic leadership

tags: politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

A call-your-representative campaign is pressing House Democrats not to hand the Speaker's gavel to Hakeem Jeffries without a competitive leadership vote in January. Organisers argue that voters who gave Democrats the House expect an open process rather than a coronation. Jeffries is running unopposed with support from progressives including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Pramila Jayapal, and has said leadership selection is an internal matter for House members.

2026 midterms were the most expensive in US history at $11.9 billion

tags: politics, markets
sources: @groundnews

Candidates, parties and outside groups spent $11.9 billion on the 2026 midterms, with $5.45 billion backing Republicans, $5.02 billion backing Democrats and $1.4 billion from independents and issue groups. Spending has roughly tripled since 2006, a rise dated to the Supreme Court's 2010 Citizens United ruling. At $96.57 per voter, U.S. spending far exceeds other democracies, with Australia next at about $19. California's Proposition 40, a one-time 5% wealth tax on the state's roughly 200 billionaires, was the most expensive ballot measure and was rejected 52.4% to 47.6% after $161 million in opposition spending led by a group founded by Sergey Brin.

Washington teachers union sues to block transgender school sports ban

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Washington's teachers union, the nonprofit TransFamilies and parents of student athletes sued the state to block Initiative 638, which bars transgender girls from competing on girls' school teams, and asked King County Superior Court to halt it before it takes effect 3 December. Plaintiffs say requiring girls to verify their sex to play school sports violates their privacy and breaches state antidiscrimination law and constitutional guarantees of equal rights and equal access to education. The measure passed on 3 November with about 56% support, with backers saying it would make competition fair for girls.

Federal judge orders Iowa to let Satanic Temple hold Capitol event

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Chief District Judge Stephanie M. Rose ruled that Iowa must grant the Satanic Temple's Iowa chapter a permit for a one-day holiday gathering in the Capitol rotunda, giving the state seven days to approve it. The group had sued alleging religious discrimination after officials denied its requests, and the judge found it had a strong chance of winning its free speech claim. State officials argued Krampus costumes could scare children and that stick props could serve as weapons; the judge said the props could pass through standard security screening. Attorney General Brenna Bird's office said the state plans to appeal.

Spain extends eviction protections and caps some rents

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Spain's interim lower chamber passed a housing decree 35-34 on Thursday, shielding vulnerable tenants from eviction through 2030 where regional authorities cannot rehouse them, freezing rents above neighbourhood benchmarks and barring real estate firms from buying properties below 70% of their value. Lawmakers rejected a second decree that would have let tenants renew leases without a time limit. The conservative Popular Party vowed to repeal the measure if it wins the 29 November election. Protests followed the October eviction and death of an 87-year-old Madrid woman, and a nationwide general strike returned the issue to the streets.

Beijing bans drone ownership across the municipality

tags: surveillance, politics
sources: @groundnews

Beijing began enforcing a ban on owning or storing drones on 15 November across its 16,400-square-kilometre municipality, including rural districts, with authorities saying the measure safeguards the security of the capital. Residents caught with drones face fines and confiscation, and bringing drones or parts into the city is prohibited; owners had to sell or relocate their devices before enforcement began. The city halted drone sales in May 2026 and had allowed registered owners to keep their devices. Exemptions can be granted for uses including policing, disaster response and farming.

Bomb found and neutralised at Illinois ethanol plant

tags: legal, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Police said a large bomb was discovered at the Bio-Urja Renewables facility in Peoria, Illinois, and has been neutralised. Authorities, members of Congress and the FBI confirmed the find, and searches continue for other possible explosives. No one was injured and evacuations in the area remain in place.

Pentagon renames AI office the Super Intelligence Office

tags: tech, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Defense Department has redesignated its Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office as the Super Intelligence Office, according to Breaking Defense. The department said the change does not alter the office's mission, leadership or budget. It follows a September order from Trump replacing the term "artificial intelligence" with "super intelligence" across the federal government.

Hegseth revives OSS name for special operations oversight

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Pentagon is reviving the Office of Strategic Services, the World War II spy agency, to oversee special operations. According to a Pentagon release, the renamed office is given under secretary level rank, at least $45 million a year and 100 dedicated billets. The original OSS was the forerunner of the CIA.

Saudi court sentences Kenyan domestic worker to 100 lashes

tags: legal
sources: @groundnews

Three Saudi judges sentenced Esther Wanja Muthoni, a 40-year-old Kenyan domestic worker, to 100 lashes in October after convicting her of sex outside marriage, basing the punishment on their reading of Islamic law. Police detained her for questioning after a supervisor took her and her newborn to a hospital in August 2025, according to court records reviewed by the New York Times. She has spent more than a year trying to return to Kenya with her one-year-old son, and the case has prevented them from leaving.

Dark money questions raised over political creator network Chorus

tags: media, politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Chorus, a creator group co-founded by Brian Tyler Cohen and Stuart Perlmutter, is registered as a 501(c)(4), meaning it is not required to disclose its donors, and its own participants say they do not know who funds it. The group says it has roughly 200 creators, does not publish their names, and asks members not to discuss program details; Cohen has described its work as including message coordination. Its sister organisation Good Influence is a for-profit influencer marketing firm whose payments are traceable in FEC filings, which show Haley Stevens' Senate campaign, a recipient of $30.6 million from AIPAC, paid Good Influence $10,000 for social media consulting in October 2025. Critics are calling for legislation requiring creators to disclose paid political content.

Connecticut offers first responders up to $25,000 toward home purchases

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Governor Ned Lamont announced that Connecticut will offer certified firefighters, police officers and emergency medical workers up to $25,000 for down payments and closing costs starting 16 November, with no income cap. Applicants must have lived and worked in the state for at least two years and buy a home in the community they serve. The state's emergency services commissioner said Connecticut needs hundreds of officers and troopers and struggles to fill its academies, and a May 2025 comptroller's report found volunteer firefighter ranks had shrunk by more than 62% since 2017.

Kentucky magistrate race decided by coin toss

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Democrat Kristen Gifford Fryman won a coin toss for the District 2 magistrate seat in Robertson County, Kentucky after she and Republican Benny Ray Renner each received 91 votes. The state election board recommended the toss, the third such tiebreaker in Kentucky this year. Fryman will join the fiscal court, which sets the county budget and tax rates.

Marine training center director relieved of command after political speech dispute

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

An unverified account circulating among service members says the director of the Tactical Training Exercise Control Group, Col. Meador, was relieved of command after a confrontation at a ball where a guest speaker delivered what amounted to a political campaign for himself. The account says a senior officer confronted the speaker, who took offence. No further details have been confirmed.
